issues.title: Internal class missing sealed keyword
issues.description: Internal implementation classes that are not designed for inheritance must be marked with the 'sealed' keyword. The WebSocketWrapper class is an internal implementation class that should be sealed to prevent unintended subclassing.
issues.rule_name: Sealed Keyword Required for Internal Implementation Classes

issues.title: Incorrect boolean operator in regex validation
issues.description: The test assertion uses AND (&&) operator instead of OR (||) when checking if the log message matches either the old or new CSP error pattern. This causes the test to fail because a log message cannot simultaneously match both regex patterns - they represent different browser error message formats. The original intent was to accept either format, but the AND operator requires both patterns to match at the same time, which is impossible. This will cause the test to fail even when receiving a valid CSP error message in either format.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
Assert.True(
    ParseErrorMessageRegexOld.IsMatch(logs[0].Message) &&
    ParseErrorMessageRegexNew.IsMatch(logs[0].Message),
    $"Expected log message to match one of the CSP error patterns: {ParseErrorMessageRegexOld} or {ParseErrorMessageRegexNew}. Actual: {logs[0].Message}");

issues.title: Disposal order causing potential race condition
issues.description: The connection disposal order is reversed - disposing secondConnection before the connection that is still being used. In the test, 'connection' performs an InvokeAsync call and its TaskCompletionSource (tcs) is awaited immediately before disposal. However, disposing secondConnection first may cause premature cleanup of shared resources or message handlers since both connections share the same user ('*'). This can lead to flaky test behavior where the connection's pending operations are interrupted by the disposal of secondConnection, especially in distributed scenarios where both connections interact with the same Redis backplane.

issues.title: Race condition from premature TaskCompletionSource recreation
issues.description: The _receiveTcs TaskCompletionSource is recreated before checking if the buffer is zero-sized, creating a race condition in the WebSocketWrapper's ReceiveAsync implementation. When a zero-byte read occurs (buffer.Count == 0), the method returns early with the result but the TCS has already been reset. This means if another thread or the background task tries to set a result on the now-recreated TCS while this zero-byte read is in progress, it will affect the next receive operation rather than completing the current one. This breaks the synchronization contract and can cause message loss or out-of-order receives in the stateful reconnection test scenarios where WebSocket message sequencing is critical.

issues.title: Test method missing Arrange/Act/Assert comments
issues.description: The modified test method does not contain explicit '// Arrange', '// Act', and '// Assert' (or '// Act & Assert') comments to delineate phases, violating the required AAA comment pattern.
issues.rule_name: Test Methods Must Use Arrange-Act-Assert Pattern with Comments

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64685 - [release/9.0] Update dependencies from dotnet/arcade

structured_output.summary:
This is a Maestro-style Arcade dependency bump (9.0.0-beta.25562.4 → 9.0.0-beta.25626.6). It updates Version.Details.xml, Versions.props and global.json, and brings in the matching eng/common script changes (the -UseBasicParsing flag, more tolerant VS requirement lookup, the 1es-azurelinux-3 image, the ci.dot.net feed, and a main-only default condition for source-index). Those parts are mechanical and look consistent.

The PR also carries hand-written test edits, and one of them is a real bug. In WebSocketCompressionTests.cs the old single regex assertion was replaced with a check that requires both the "old" and "new" Chrome CSP message patterns to match (&&). The two patterns are mutually exclusive, so the assertion can never pass and the blocked-compression E2E tests will always fail. The Redis test changes (quarantines, dispose order, TCS reset moved earlier) are plausible flakiness mitigations but are unrelated to the dependency update.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `&&` in the WebSocket compression E2E assertion makes the test unsatisfiable, so it fails on every browser version. The rest is a routine dependency bump.

architecture.overview:
The repo pins its build tooling (Arcade SDK, Helix SDK, installers/templating tasks, RemoteExecutor) in eng/Version.Details.xml, eng/Versions.props and global.json. The eng/common folder is a verbatim copy of Arcade's shared scripts and pipeline templates. This PR is the Maestro flow that bumps those pins to a newer Arcade build and refreshes the eng/common copy.

On top of the automated change, the PR includes edits to two test files: an E2E CSP error-message assertion for blocked WebSocket compression, and the Redis SignalR end-to-end tests (quarantines, a dispose-order swap and a receive-TCS reset change in a test WebSocket wrapper).
steps: Start at global.json, Versions.props and Version.Details.xml: all Arcade-sourced packages move to 9.0.0-beta.25626.6 with the new Arcade SHA.

eng/common PowerShell: tools.ps1, internal-feed-operations.ps1 and nuget-verification.ps1 add -UseBasicParsing to Invoke-WebRequest, and LocateVisualStudio tolerates a missing tools.vs entry in global.json.
eng/common pipeline templates: the source-build image becomes 1es-azurelinux-3, the internal runtime feed becomes ci.dot.net, and the source-index-stage1 condition defaults to main-only.
WebSocketCompressionTests.cs: the single generated regex becomes two (old and new Chrome CSP wording), combined in the assertion.
RedisEndToEnd.cs: two theories are quarantined, the dispose order is swapped, WebSocketWrapper is unsealed, and the receive TCS is reset before the zero-byte check.

findings.title: Assertion requires both mutually exclusive CSP patterns to match (&& instead of ||)
findings.fixPrompt: In src/Components/test/E2ETest/ServerExecutionTests/WebSocketCompressionTests.cs (~lines 107-110), the Assert.True combines ParseErrorMessageRegexOld.IsMatch and ParseErrorMessageRegexNew.IsMatch with `&&`. The two patterns are mutually exclusive, so the assertion can never pass. Change `&&` to `||` so the test accepts either the old or new Chrome CSP message wording. Keep the failure message as is.

findings.title: Unrelated Redis test changes bundled into a dependency bump
findings.fixPrompt: In src/SignalR/server/StackExchangeRedis/test/RedisEndToEnd.cs, WebSocketWrapper (line ~362) was changed from `sealed` to non-sealed, and ReceiveAsync (lines ~406-417) now resets `_receiveTcs` before the zero-byte early return. Confirm whether both changes are intended. If unsealing has no consumer, restore `sealed`. Add a comment explaining why the TCS is reset before the zero-byte check, or move these test changes to a separate PR.

findings.title: Arcade bump itself is mechanical and consistent
findings.body: All six Arcade packages use the same version and SHA across Version.Details.xml, Versions.props and global.json. The eng/common changes (-UseBasicParsing, null-safe `tools.vs` handling, new pool image and feed) match upstream Arcade. The source-index-stage1 default condition now restricts the job to main. That should be harmless on release/9.0 but is worth knowing about.
